articles.title: ‘Gondhal’ director Santosh Davakhar on India’s Oscar entry, Diwali release in 7 languages and more: ''Ramayana' would give our film more room' - Exclusive
articles.summary: Marathi cinema is increasingly finding its place in the national conversation, but taking regional stories to a wider audience comes with its own set of
articles.body: Marathi cinema is increasingly finding its place in the national conversation, but taking regional stories to a wider audience comes with its own set of challenges. Director Santosh Davakhar hopes to bridge that gap with ‘Gondhal’, a psychological thriller rooted in Maharashtra’s cultural traditions that blends devotion, deception, desire and betrayal. Selected as India’s official entry for the 99th Academy Awards, the film is set for a worldwide release in seven languages on November 13, following the arrival of ‘Ramayana’ on November 5.For Davakhar, the film represents an opportunity to introduce Maharashtra’s cultural heritage to audiences beyond the Marathi-speaking world while demonstrating the universal appeal of stories rooted in regional identities. From retaining the authenticity of a traditional ritual across multiple language versions to navigating marketing challenges, theatrical distribution and the struggle for screens, the filmmaker believes that strong storytelling and audience support are essential for Marathi cinema to grow.The director also opens up about the responsibility of representing India on the international stage, why he believes ‘Gondhal’ deserves to be experienced in theatres, and how the Oscar campaign has temporarily put his next project, ‘Shahaji Raje’, on hold. In this conversation, Davakhar shares his vision for the future of Marathi cinema, including his ambitious dream of seeing the industry achieve ₹1,000 crore in annual box-office collections within the next five years.‘Gondhal’ is releasing worldwide in seven languages on November 13, shortly after ‘Ramayana’ on November 5. How significant is this release window, and does the pan-India ambition bring added expectations?We originally wanted a Diwali release. With ‘Ramayana’ arriving on November 5 and the excitement surrounding it, we felt November 13 would give our film more room. By the following week, audiences may be ready for a different experience. Releasing worldwide in seven languages is a big step for us. It brings expectations, but also the hope that our Marathi story will connect with a much wider audience. Their support can strengthen our Oscar campaign too.The film’s trailer has now been released globally. What was the central thought behind the story, and what do you hope audiences take away from it?From the beginning, I wanted to tell a story rooted in Maharashtra that could represent India internationally. I spoke about that dream even a year before the film’s release. ‘Gondhal’ brings together devotion, deception, desire and betrayal. A sacred ritual becomes the setting for a psychological thriller. I want audiences to feel the suspense and leave thinking about the characters, their choices and the consequences.Taking a Marathi film to audiences across seven languages is a big step. How challenging was it to retain its cultural authenticity while making it accessible to viewers from different regions?The challenge was to make the dialogue feel natural in every language while preserving Marathi culture, traditional music and the village atmosphere. At its heart, the film explores complex human emotions such as jealousy, greed, the struggle for power and obsession. These emotions connect with people everywhere. Audiences may be unfamiliar with the ritual, but they will understand the characters and what drives them.With ‘Gondhal’ drawing attention as India’s official entry for the 99th Academy Awards, how has that recognition influenced your approach to presenting it internationally?Being India’s official entry makes international audiences take notice, but it also brings responsibility. India is a diverse country, with rich traditions in every corner. Through ‘Gondhal’, we are trying to preserve and share one of those traditions. We want international audiences to discover this culture through its people and their story. Representing our culture, our community and our country together is a huge honour and a dream come true.What sets ‘Gondhal’ apart from other films releasing around the same time, and why should audiences experience it in theatres?‘Gondhal’ is completely a team effort. Every head of department and every team member has contributed to its quality. The FFI jury told us they chose the film because it was the best across departments, including acting. That appreciation belongs to the whole team. Some of our actors may not be famous faces, but they deliver powerful performances.The 25-minute opening take, unpredictable twists, visuals and live sound draw you into a remote village in Maharashtra and make you feel part of its world. Please watch it in theatres. That is where you can fully experience everyone’s work together. We created it for the big screen, and we are not currently planning an OTT release.How important is marketing for a Marathi film today, especially when competing with big-budget Hindi and South Indian releases?Marketing is essential because even a good film needs to reach people. We are a small production house, so we must use our resources carefully while putting quality first. Today’s audiences know what they want: a strong story and a fresh experience. Our marketing must make them curious enough to buy a ticket. After that, the film must earn their appreciation. Word of mouth can become our strongest support.Could your next film also be rooted in Marathi culture, or are you looking to tell a story with a more pan-India setting?My next film, ‘Shahaji Raje’, is rooted in Maharashtra’s history and pride. The screenplay and dialogues are ready, and we were preparing to begin shooting. We have now put it on hold for three to four months to give ‘Gondhal’ and its Oscar campaign our complete attention. India has given us a big responsibility, and we want to give it our best. I believe a story rooted in Maharashtra can still connect with audiences across the country.What is one change you would like to see in the Marathi film industry over the next five years?I would love to see a stronger bond between Marathi films and their audiences. It must be a two-way effort: filmmakers need to create fresh, engaging stories, and audiences need to support them in theatres. My dream is that, within the next five years, Marathi cinema reaches ₹1,000 crore in annual box-office collections. That growth would create opportunities for new talent, more stories and ambitious films.A Marathi film can win awards and represent India at the Oscars, but can it get enough screens at home? How do you respond to that contradiction?It is a real concern. International recognition does not automatically bring enough screens or suitable showtimes at home. But our limited Hindi paid previews received an encouraging response. At our Pune screening, even tourists took time out of their visit to watch the film and came away happy. That gives me confidence.Kannada cinema faced similar challenges before a few major successes helped it reach audiences across India. I believe Marathi cinema can do the same. This year, ‘Krantijyoti Vidyalay Marathi Madhyam’, ‘Deool Band 2’ and ‘Raja Shivaji’ together have done around ₹250 crore in worldwide business. Their success shows the strength of stories rooted in our culture. We need to build on that momentum and give more Marathi films a fair chance to reach their audiences.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Halloween watchlist: 20  films from the 21st century that reshaped horror
articles.body: 1. Don’t Breathe (2016)Director: Fede ÁlvarezThree young burglars break into the home of a war veteran, believing that his isolation makes him an easy target. Rocky hopes to use the stolen money to escape her abusive home, while her companions see the robbery as a quick financial opportunity. Their plan collapses…Fede Álvarez builds suspense through precise spatial choreography and carefully controlled silence. Although the increasingly extreme twists occasionally strain credibility, the film remains an effective examination of desperation, moral compromise and the dangers of underestimating someone because they appear vulnerable.2. Goodnight Mommy (2014)Directors: Veronika Franz and Severin FialaTwin brothers Elias and Lukas return home to find their mother recovering from facial surgery, her head covered in bandages. Expecting affection and familiarity, they instead encounter a woman who behaves coldly, imposes strict rules and seems emotionally distant. Gradually, the boys become convinced that she is an impostor who has replaced their real mother.Ordinary disagreements become increasingly disturbing as the twins subject the woman to cruel tests intended to establish her identity. The directors encourage viewers to share the children's uncertainty, making it difficult to distinguish genuine evidence from the products of fear and imagination.3. Good Boy (2025)Director: Ben LeonbergTold largely from the perspective of a dog named Indy, Good Boy follows his attempts to protect his human companion, Todd, after they move into a secluded family home. Todd's health is deteriorating, and the property appears to harbour a disturbing supernatural presence. Indy senses danger in empty rooms, unfamiliar shadows and strange sounds that the humans cannot fully understand.The film’s unusual perspective creates suspense without relying on conventional dialogue or exposition. Indy cannot explain what he sees, so his fear emerges through barking, body language, hesitation and his determination to remain near Todd. The audience is left to interpret the threat through the same limited information available to the animal.4. A Quiet Place (2018)Director: John KrasinskiIn a devastated America, a family struggles to survive among blind creatures that hunt through sound. Lee and Evelyn Abbott and their children communicate through sign language, walk carefully along prepared paths and suppress every avoidable noise. Their elaborate precautions reflect a world where even a small mistake can prove fatal.John Krasinski transforms silence into the film's central dramatic device. Footsteps, creaking floorboards and unexpected noises acquire extraordinary significance. The monsters provide the external threat, but the emotional story concerns parental responsibility, grief and the difficulties of protecting children without being able to control every danger.5. Get Out (2017)Director: Jordan PeeleChris Washington, a photographer, accompanies his girlfriend, Rose, to meet her parents at their country estate. Their apparently progressive hospitality soon becomes unsettling, particularly when the household’s Black employees behave strangely and the family's wealthy guests display an uncomfortable fascination with Chris's body and physical abilities. Jordan Peele gradually transforms social awkwardness into psychological horror.6. Knock at the Cabin (2023)Director: M. Night ShyamalanEric and Andrew are vacationing with their young daughter, Wen, when four strangers arrive at their secluded cabin. Led by Leonard, the visitors insist that the family must make an unbearable choice: one of the two men must willingly die to prevent an impending apocalypse.Shyamalan confines much of the action to the cabin, allowing the characters' limited knowledge to generate tension. Dave Bautista is particularly effective as Leonard, whose imposing physical presence contrasts with his apparent gentleness and anguish. The film's central dilemma is about the limits of moral responsibility: should people sacrifice someone they love for the survival of strangers, especially when certainty is impossible?7. Ginger Snaps (2000)Director: John FawcettGinger and Brigitte Fitzgerald are teenage sisters who feel alienated from their suburban surroundings and share a fascination with death. Their intense bond begins to fracture when Ginger is attacked by a mysterious creature during her first menstruation. She survives, but her body and personality begin changing in disturbing ways.Ginger becomes more assertive and sexually confident, attracting attention from boys while growing increasingly aggressive. The werewolf mythology gives physical form to anxieties about menstruation, sexuality and female adolescence. Ginger's transformation is both empowering and destructive, while Brigitte faces the painful possibility of losing the person whose identity has always been intertwined with her own.8. A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night (2014)Director: Ana Lily AmirpourSet in the fictional Iranian town of Bad City, this black-and-white film follows a nameless young woman who wanders the streets at night. She is a vampire who preys on men whose behaviour is exploitative or abusive, becoming an unsettling presence in a community marked by addiction, prostitution and neglect.Her life intersects with that of Arash, a young man struggling to care for his drug-addicted father. Their growing connection develops through shared loneliness rather than conventional romantic gestures. Both characters inhabit a world where intimacy is difficult and survival demands moral compromises.9. Cloverfield (2008)Director: Matt ReevesPresented as recovered camcorder footage, Cloverfield follows a group of young New Yorkers caught in a sudden monster attack. The disaster interrupts a farewell party for Rob Hawkins, whose personal problems initially seem far more important than the unexplained explosions shaking the city.As Manhattan descends into chaos, the group discovers that a gigantic creature is attacking buildings and destroying streets. The found-footage format restricts the audience to what the characters can see and understand. The shaky camera, fragmented information and sudden changes in direction recreate the confusion of civilians experiencing a disaster without knowing its cause.10. I Saw the Devil (2010)Director: Kim Jee-woonWhen his pregnant fiancée is murdered by serial killer Jang Kyung-chul, intelligence agent Kim Soo-hyun embarks on a personal campaign of revenge. The pursuit becomes an increasingly disturbing contest between two men whose actions draw them towards the same moral darkness. This movie is an uncompromising psychological thriller about grief, obsession and the corruption of moral purpose.11. The Host (2006)Director: Bong Joon HoA monstrous creature emerges from Seoul's Han River after toxic chemicals are improperly disposed of in a laboratory. During an attack on the riverbank, it abducts Hyun-seo, the young daughter of Park Gang-du, who runs a snack kiosk nearby. Her family is devastated, but their attempts to rescue her are complicated by authorities who impose quarantine and insist that the creature carries a dangerous virus.Bong combines creature horror with dark comedy and social satire, linking the disaster to environmental negligence and institutional failure. The monster is frighteningly physical, but the film's emotional centre remains the family's refusal to abandon a missing child.12. Crimson Peak (2015)Director: Guillermo del ToroEdith Cushing, an aspiring writer fascinated by ghost stories, falls in love with Thomas Sharpe, an English aristocrat seeking financial support for an invention. Despite her father's reservations, she marries Thomas and moves to his ancestral mansion, Allerdale Hall, a decaying Gothic structure that appears to be sinking into the surrounding red clay.Living there with Thomas and his possessive sister Lucille, Edith begins experiencing disturbing supernatural manifestations. Guillermo del Toro builds the film around the visual traditions of Gothic romance. Elaborate costumes, stark colours and grotesque supernatural imagery make the mansion an essential part of the storytelling. Crimson Peak explores the disturbing possibility that the people who claim to love us may also be the ones most capable of destroying us.13. The Orphanage (2007)Director: J. A. BayonaLaura returns to the former orphanage where she grew up, intending to reopen it as a home for children with special needs. She arrives with her husband, Carlos, and their adopted son, Simón, whose mysterious imaginary companions begin to unsettle the household.During a gathering at the property, Simón disappears. Laura launches a desperate search, convinced that the old building contains clues to his whereabouts. As the police investigation fails to provide answers, she becomes increasingly absorbed in the orphanage's history and the possibility that the children who once lived there have left behind a supernatural presence.Bayona uses the house's corridors, locked rooms and concealed spaces to build suspense without relying excessively on graphic violence. The mystery gradually becomes inseparable from Laura's grief and determination to find her son.14. Annihilation (2018)Director: Alex GarlandBiologist Lena joins an expedition into the Shimmer, an expanding and unexplained phenomenon surrounding an isolated coastal region. Her husband, Kane, has returned from an earlier mission physically deteriorating and unable to explain what happened inside. Determined to understand his condition, Lena enters the affected zone with a team of scientists.Within the Shimmer, the natural world behaves in increasingly disturbing ways. Plants grow in human-like forms, animals mutate and familiar biological boundaries dissolve as DNA appears to be rearranged. The expedition members also experience psychological disturbances, making it difficult to separate external threats from their own vulnerabilities.Garland combines science-fiction spectacle with cosmic horror, creating an environment that resists ordinary explanation. The Shimmer also functions as a metaphor for self-destruction, grief and the human desire to escape painful aspects of existence.15. The Descent (2005)Director: Neil MarshallA year after losing her husband and daughter in an accident, Sarah joins five female friends on a caving expedition. The trip is intended to help her reconnect with them, but the adventure turns disastrous when a collapse blocks their route out of an unexplored cave system.Their predicament becomes far worse when they encounter subterranean humanoid creatures adapted to life in darkness. The group must improvise weapons, conserve supplies and search for an escape route while being hunted underground.The monsters are not the only source of danger. Secrets and betrayals within the group intensify existing tensions, while Sarah's grief gradually gives way to a more aggressive determination to survive. The Descent is a ferocious survival horror film in which physical terror and psychological collapse reinforce each other.16. Shaun of the Dead (2004)Director: Edgar WrightShaun is an underachieving electronics salesman whose life revolves around his best friend Ed, their local pub and a deteriorating relationship with his girlfriend Liz. When Liz leaves him, Shaun is forced to confront his lack of direction. At the same time, a zombie outbreak begins spreading through London.Edgar Wright combines horror conventions with tightly edited visual comedy and affectionate references to classic zombie cinema. The undead also function as a satire of everyday inertia, their repetitive movements reflecting the routines that have trapped Shaun in an unsatisfying life. Beneath the comedy lies a coming-of-age story about responsibility and friendship.17. The Witch (2015)Director: Robert EggersIn seventeenth-century New England, a deeply religious family is expelled from its Puritan settlement and establishes an isolated farm beside a vast forest. William, his wife Katherine and their children believe that strict faith and hard work will protect them, but their fragile existence collapses when their youngest child disappears while under the care of his older sister, Thomasin.The family begins suspecting witchcraft as further disturbing events unfold.Eggers recreates the period through archaic dialogue, historical detail and a restrained visual style. The horror emerges from the collision between religious certainty and a reality that refuses easy explanation.18. The Conjuring (2013)Director: James WanThe Perron family moves into an isolated Rhode Island farmhouse during the 1970s, hoping for a fresh start. Strange events soon disrupt their lives: clocks stop, unexplained noises echo through the house, objects move. The disturbances gradually become more violent, particularly for Carolyn Perron and her five daughters.Desperate for help, Carolyn contacts paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren. Wan builds suspense through careful sound design, dark corridors and concealed spaces. Rather than immediately revealing every supernatural presence, he encourages viewers to anticipate danger in the edges of the frame.The story's central conflict is ultimately about protection. Carolyn's determination to save her children drives the narrative, while Ed and Lorraine's partnership provides a counterpoint to the fear surrounding them.19. Let the Right One In (2008)Director: Tomas AlfredsonOskar is a lonely twelve-year-old boy living in a bleak Stockholm suburb, where he endures persistent bullying at school. His life changes when Eli, an unusual girl, moves into the neighbouring apartment with an older man. Although Eli initially insists that they cannot be friends, the two children gradually develop a bond built on their shared isolation.As mysterious killings disturb the neighbourhood, Oskar discovers something chilling. Alfredson uses snow-covered courtyards, dimly lit apartments and sparse dialogue to create an atmosphere of profound melancholy. The horror is often graphic, but the film's central concern is emotional rather than sensational.20. 28 Days Later (2002)Director: Danny BoyleJim, a bicycle courier, awakens from a coma to discover that London has been abandoned following a devastating viral outbreak. The infection, known as Rage, spreads through bodily fluids and transforms its victims into violently aggressive carriers. Unlike traditional slow-moving zombies, the infected sprint towards their prey, making every encounter immediate and terrifying.Jim joins survivors Selena, Frank and Frank's daughter Hannah as they attempt to reach a reported military refuge.Danny Boyle’s grainy digital cinematography gives the empty city a haunting immediacy, while rapid editing intensifies the infected attacks.28 Days Later helped reinvent modern zombie cinema by combining fast-moving infected, urban desolation and a bleak examination of how catastrophe exposes both human cruelty and the need for connection.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Katrina Kaif breaks silence on the scrutiny around her post-partum weight: 'People are aware of what a woman's body goes through, it's their choice if they still view it through a harsh lens'
articles.summary: Katrina Kaif has spoken out against the scrutiny surrounding her postpartum appearance, months after social media users commented on her changing physique
articles.body: Katrina Kaif has spoken out against the scrutiny surrounding her postpartum appearance, months after social media users commented on her changing physique following childbirth. The actor, who made her first major public appearance in months alongside husband Vicky Kaushal at the Ambani family's annual Ganesh Chaturthi on September 14, became the subject of online comparisons after photographs from the event surfaced.Soon after the couple's appearance, social media was flooded with 'before and after' and 'then and now' collages comparing Katrina's pre-pregnancy pictures with her recent photographs. The comparisons drew criticism for placing unrealistic expectations on women to regain their pre-pregnancy bodies soon after giving birth. Several women also called out the body shaming directed at the actor and questioned society's obsession with women's appearances after motherhood.Katrina addressed the online commentary, speaking about the changes a woman's body undergoes after childbirth and the pressure to conform to societal expectations.She said in an interview with Vogue India, "We live in a world that wants to blow us around in the ever-changing winds of opinions. I think most people are aware of what a woman’s body goes through after giving birth. And if they still choose to view that body through a harsh lens, it’s a personal choice. It can’t be blamed on a lack of information, because there is so much information out there. I just want to focus on this lovely part of my life and where I’m headed."The actor also challenged the widely used phrase 'bounce back', questioning why women are expected to return to their pre-pregnancy bodies as though childbirth were something to recover from.Katrina said, "Bounce back? From where? I have taken a step ahead to something that was a deep desire in my heart, so why would I want to go back? The first few days after I gave birth, it was an indescribable feeling to see Vihaan’s face and know that four years of a tumultuous journey for me and Vicky had led to this. I am very aware of my fitness journey and where my body feels at its most energetic. I will reach there at my own pace."The interview further quoted Naomi Wolf, from her 1990 book The Beauty Myth where she said, “Whatever is deeply, essentially female—the life in a woman’s expression, the feel of her flesh, the shape of her breasts, the transformations after childbirth of her skin—is being reclassified as ugly, and ugliness as disease.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: La noticia ha dado, por desgracia, la vuelta al mundo Ouigo suspende todas sus circulaciones entre Madrid y Andalucía al menos hasta el 2 de noviembre
articles.body:
Última hora del accidente de tren, en directo:

En la mañana del miércoles 28 de octubre, a las 8:34 horas, ha tenido lugar un accidente entre dos trenes de alta velocidad. Un AVE de Renfe y un Iryo han colisionado, provocando que por lo menos dos de los vagones salieran desprendidos por un terraplen entre las localidades de Los Yébenes y Urda, situadas en la provincia de Toledo.

Hay confirmados 68 fallecidos y más de 50 heridos. Además de que está cerrada la línea entre Madrid y Andalucía.

El Ministro de Transportes ha catalogado de "inexplicable" lo sucedido y ha tratado de explicar lo que se sabe hasta ahora del accidente. Hubo un problema en el sistema LBZ, se detuvieron todos los trenes que habían en el tramo de 55 kilómetros, entró entonces el centro de control de Renfe y dio permiso para reanudar a marcha normal uno de los trenes, que transcurrió por 25 kilómetros a unos 200 km/hora y ese es el tren Renfe que terminaría colisionando. articles.title: Spain train crash: What we know after two trains collide with dozens feared dead
articles.summary: More than 500 passengers were on board the trains when the incident occurred in the province of Toledo, south of Madrid.
articles.body:
Two trains have collided in Spain just south of the capital Madrid on Wednesday morning.

Rail operator Adif says the incident occurred between a Renfe train and another of the Iryo company, which covers the Madrid to Seville route.

So far at least 68 people are confirmed to have died in the incident.

Here is what we know about the crash so far.

The two trains collided just after 09:00 (08:00 GMT) between municipalities Mora and Orgaz, and about 140km (100 miles) south of Madrid.

The accident happened when a high-speed train travelling from Madrid to the south of the country collided with another train that was apparently stationary. The crash caused at least two carriages to fall down an embankment.

Broadcaster RTVE, quoting the transport ministry, said a Renfe train rear-ended an Iryo train.

Renfe is Spain's national state-owned railway company while Iryo is a private high-speed railway operator.

All train traffic on this line has been stopped at stations along the route, Adif said.

Renfe said services between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia remain suspended.

A passenger on board one of the trains told local media there was a heavy impact about 40 minutes into the journey.

Iryo said its train was "struck from behind" by a Renfe train "due to causes that are still unknown.

Transport minister Oscar Puente has said a computer failure led to the initial halt of six moving trains, including the two trains that subsequently collided.

"In the event of a system failure, the control centre takes over," he said, adding it was the control centre which decided to allow the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions.

That decision, Puente said, was made "under inexplicable circumstances". It resulted in the Renfe train crashing into the Iryo train, which was stationary on the tracks further ahead.

More than 500 people were believed to be on board both trains.

Esther Padilla, spokesperson for the government of Castilla-La Mancha region, told TVE that one of the trains - managed by the Iryo company - was carrying 146 passengers plus one baby, while the Renfe-managed train had 397 passengers on board.

A former government minister was also among those reported missing.

The Spanish Confederation of Business Organizations (CEOE) posted on X that, Fátima Báñez - who heads the organization's foundation - was on board one of the trains involved in the crash.

The Castilla La Mancha regional government said 64 people are now confirmed to have died.

Speaking separately to Spanish media, he warned the death toll could increase further.

Eighty people are being treated for injuries, according to authorities, with 50 of the casualties said to be in a serious condition , and 15 more in a critical condition.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has said "the whole of Spain is grieving" and that "lives have been shattered, families have been torn apart".

"The pain is immense," he said on a visit to the crash site.

The government was "trying to determine what was the origin of this tragedy, of this terrible accident," he added.

"We will get to the bottom of this, and if there has been any negligence, it will come to light.

"If there have been failures in the security system, they will be addressed with the utmost firmness."

Sánchez and other Spanish politicians have cancelled all public engagements on Wednesday, including campaigning for next month's parliamentary elections.

Spain's royal family posted on X that it was "shocked and concerned" and expressed condolences for the relatives of the deceased and those affected by the crash.

A spokesperson for the EU said the bloc was ready to help Spain if needed.

A huge emergency response is under way with fire crews and helicopters at the scene.

Hospitals in the area have suspended planned surgeries as they deal with an influx of patients from the crash, Spanish media have reported.

A blood transfusion centre in Madrid has also appealed for "urgent" donations. In a post on X, Centro de Transfusión said it made the request "in the face of a possible sudden increase in care needs".

It reported that facilities in Toledo, Ciudad Real and Alcázar de San Juan have cancelled procedures as casualties from the crash begin to arrive.

This is the second high-speed rail tragedy in Spain this year.

In January a high-speed train derailed in southern Spain , its rear carriages going into the path of a state-run Renfe train, claiming the lives of 46 people.

articles.summary: Manoj Muntashir, the lyricist and dialogue writer of ‘Adipurush’, has responded to comparisons between his film’s music and the songs of ‘Ramayana’ Part 1.
articles.body: Manoj Muntashir, the lyricist and dialogue writer of ‘Adipurush’, has responded to comparisons between his film’s music and the songs of ‘Ramayana’ Part 1. The ‘Ramayana’ songs, composed by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer, have drawn mixed reactions, with many first criticising and then praising them.What Manoj Muntashir saidReacting on X to a report on the backlash to ‘Mangal Rang’, Manoj Muntashir said people were being reminded of the “stunts” in ‘Adipurush’. Adipurush was a very bad film; the dialogues were even worse, but the songs—every child in the country sings them. Go to Shri Ayodhya sometime, and you’ll hear nothing but Adipurush songs playing in every alley.”Manoj Muntashir says, ‘There was no lack of devotion’Manoj said the music of his film was made with sincerity. “The mistake I made, I’ve apologised to the Ram devotees for it countless times, and forgiveness was granted, but don’t challenge the songs. articles.title: Collin Gosselin calls out reality TV producers for putting ratings ahead of kids: 'The show must go on'
articles.summary: Collin Gosselin's memoir alleges child exploitation on "Jon & Kate Plus 8," claiming production priorities came at the expense of his well-being.
articles.body: Collin Gosselin is sounding the alarm on the reality TV industry, accusing adults of turning a blind eye when children are hurting — all to keep the cameras rolling. The "Jon & Kate Plus 8" star is revisiting the painful realities of his youth in his new memoir, "In the Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood," alleging that what made for compelling television often came at the expense of the children living it. "It's the simple fact that adults that are seeing these things, they surely understood that people are choosing not to say anything because the show must go on," Collin told Fox News Digital. 'JON & KATE PLUS 8' STAR COLLIN GOSSELIN ACCUSES MOM OF TRYING TO 'BURY' HIM TO 'PROTECT HER REPUTATION' "And if, at any point in time, a child can voice that they do not want to film, we need to take that seriously," he said. Collin, one of the sextuplets who rose to fame alongside his parents and siblings, said children should not have to clearly articulate their distress before the adults around them recognize something is wrong. "To understand and to know that at a young age, at any age, means that you really, you feel in your heart that it is not right, and you know you're being exploited and that's crazy for a child to know," he said. "But we should listen to that because that's a huge thing." WATCH HERE: COLLIN GOSSELIN CALLS OUT REALITY TV PRODUCERS FOR PUTTING RATINGS AHEAD OF KIDS Even when children remain silent, Collin argued, adults have a responsibility to pay attention. "But even without a child saying anything, you can tell, you can absolutely tell. It's reading body language," Collin said. "You can absolutely tell and we should be aware. We should be paying attention. We should be protecting children." WATCH: COLLIN GOSSELIN BLASTS MOM KATE FOR 'BURYING' HIM TO SAVE HER REPUTATION Collin said the show's production priorities came at the expense of his well-being and that of his siblings, arguing that the demands of filming conflicted with what was best for the children. "100% my entire childhood, what was best for production was this direct relationship to what was unhealthy for a child," he said. "But nobody cared about the welfare of me and my siblings, they cared about my paycheck." He also said his siblings were kept in the dark about what happened at home while they were at school, adding that he hopes they will examine his account for themselves. JON GOSSELIN CLAIMS HE'S 'PERFECT STRANGERS NOW' WITH SIX OF HIS KIDS AFTER YEARS OF NO CONTACT "A lot happened that was kept from them intentionally so that they could be told that their brother was this and that," Collin said. As filming intensified, Collin said the family's public image took priority over the children's experiences at home. "But once everything got going, and we were at the height of filming and production, it was absolutely more about what it looked like on the outside and not necessarily how me and my siblings felt," he said. "It was always about how it looked for everybody else." For Collin, the failure is not simply recognizing that something is wrong, but refusing to act. "Doing something about it because the biggest thing is when we know something's wrong, and we don't say anything that's worse than not knowing it," he said. Collin said the family that audiences watched on "Jon & Kate Plus 8" did not reflect the full reality of his childhood, arguing that viewers saw a more polished version of life at home. KATE GOSSELIN CALLED A 'MONSTER' IN SOCIAL MEDIA COMMENTS AFTER SON COLLIN ANNOUNCES MEMOIR When asked what cameras failed to capture, he described experiences and opportunities that he said were offered to the children for filming but later taken away. His criticism goes beyond editing and production decisions. Collin also revisited his experience of being placed in a treatment facility and given medication, describing a period when he felt stripped of control over his life. "For a long time, my name was dragged, and I was put away. I was essentially put in a juvenile prison, put on all these medications," he said. "I was a zombie half the time. I had no control, I had nothing." I went through the motions, and was like a zombie every day," he said. Reflecting on that experience, Collin said he feels compelled to speak publicly about what happened. "And so when you reflect on all that, you realize these things need to be talked about, and I feel just an urge to talk about them," he said. He recalled a visit from Kate when he was 13, claiming the encounter left him with a painful final memory. "She berated me for all of 20 minutes after not seeing me for over a year," he said. Meanwhile, Collin told Fox News Digital he held on to hope even during what he described as his darkest moments. "I had very little hope, but I always had some, and I hung on to that … I just kept telling myself that there's a better future for me and there will be a time where I will be past this," he said. articles.title: Javier Aroca, licenciado en Derecho, y su milagrosa salvación: "No me tocó la bola negra"
articles.standfirst: El relato de quien pudo estar en el convoy y que ha mandado un mensaje desde la televisión para calmar a todo el mundo
articles.summary: El relato de quien pudo estar en el convoy y que ha mandado un mensaje desde la televisión para calmar a todo el mundo
articles.body: El trágico accidente ferroviario ocurrido en la línea que conecta Madrid y Sevilla ha dejado una profunda huella de dolor e incertidumbre. El habitual trayecto de primera hora de la mañana, frecuentado por numerosos trabajadores y ciudadanos que se desplazan regularmente entre ambas capitales, se convirtió esta mañana en el escenario de una auténtica pesadilla. Entre los habituales de esta vía se encontraba el conocido analista, Javier Aroca, quien reconoció con evidente pesar que "la salida de atocha 10:39 debía llegar a la estación de Santa Justa", un recorrido que él mismo transita de manera constante cada semana. La conmoción inicial dio paso al desconcierto cuando familiares y allegados comenzaron a intentar contactar sin éxito con los viajeros tras conocerse la noticia. El propio tertuliano relató los angustiosos momentos vividos en las primeras horas del día debido a la falta de comunicación, señalando que "muchos amigos y mi familia se han pegado un disgusto enorme esta mañana porque no me localizadores, ¿no?". La fortuna quiso que, en esta ocasión, sus planes sufrieran una modificación de horario que evitó que se subiera al convoy siniestrado. Aunque asegura que por cuestiones personales "hoy tenía previsto volver afortunadamente a otra hora más tardía y no he tenido no me ha tocado la bola negra", decía. Visiblemente afectado por la magnitud de la tragedia, el colaborador admitió ante las cámaras que "la verdad es que no tengo mucho cuerpo de estar aquí, para que te voy a engañar", destacando que su intervención pública buscaba fundamentalmente tranquilizar a su entorno. Asimismo, quiso poner en valor el factor humano frente a la tragedia impersonal, recordando que las víctimas no son meras cifras, sino "vecinos, son ciudadanos, son trabajadores y esto duelen mucho". Frente al dolor colectivo, el analista quiso alzar la voz para reivificar la labor de los profesionales del sector ferroviario. En este sentido, defendió con firmeza la dedicación de quienes operan estas líneas y subrayó que "estos viajes casi siempre funcionan muy bien", desmarcándose de discursos alarmistas y exigiendo rigor y humanidad en el tratamiento de la catástrofe. Finalmente, ante la gravedad de los hechos, se incidió en la necesidad imperiosa de esclarecer los motivos exactos del suceso. Con un llamamiento a la rápida actuación de los equipos técnicos y periciales, se concluyó que "espero que la investigación vuele, como como vuela el AVE y vuela el Iryo" para aportar paz y certidumbre a la sociedad.

articles.title: TikTok is going after Yelp and Google Maps with an in-app restaurant guide
articles.summary: TikTok is adding a new Yelp-like feature to its app, where users can find and review local restaurants, as well as see content associated with businesses.
articles.body: TikTok is launching an in-app restaurant guide in a challenge to other platforms like Yelp and even Google Maps. The company on Wednesday announced the launch of Must Eat, a new section of the TikTok app built on 40 million posts, reviews, and comments about dining on the platform. The new feature uses videos and discussions of buzzy local businesses to create restaurant recommendation guides. Users can leave reviews of restaurants, call and make reservations, and search for nearby businesses on a map. At a launch event this week, TikTok US CEO Adam Presser called Must Eat “the compilation of all of the conversation that’s happening on the TikTok platform across creators, restaurateurs, [and] individuals” who make videos or leave comments about local restaurants. Among the featured restaurants in New York are Golden Diner (home of very viral pancakes) and hard-to-reserve spots like Semma and Via Carota. Must Eat falls somewhere between Yelp and more curated recommendations from publications like The Infatuation. Must Eat is divided into two category tabs: “everyday eats” and “elevated dining.” Users can sort and filter by rating, distance, cuisine type, and what’s currently open, and each page for a restaurant links to videos about the business posted to TikTok. Diners can also bookmark businesses to save them for later. The feature is initially available in a few select regions — New York City, Los Angeles, and the Bay Area. The company says restaurants can’t pay to be featured in the recommendation lists. It’s not the first time TikTok has tried to bridge the gap for users between seeing a video about a place and actually visiting in person. Earlier this year, the company added the ability to book hotels and attractions through the app. That feature, TikTok Go, allowed content creators to tag and link to locations; Must Eat is an expansion of that earlier capability. TikTok’s deeper move into the dining space is fitting, given the app’s profound impact on restaurants. Content creators have angled to become the food critics of the short-form video era, each with their own schtick or eccentricities. The popularity of food videos has even changed what restaurants put on the menu to begin with, like extra-long cheese pulls or dramatic presentations. In its press release announcing the launch of Must Eat, TikTok says 27 million US diners went to a restaurant, cafe, or shop for the first time thanks to the platform last year.

articles.title: Jennifer Lawrence finally confirms 'Hunger Games' return with 'Sunrise on the Reaping' role
articles.summary: The actor, who plays Katniss Everdeen in the dystopian franchise, has confirmed she's back alongside Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson.
articles.body:
After nearly a year of speculation, Jennifer Lawrence has confirmed that she features in the upcoming Hunger Games movie, Sunrise on the Reaping .

The actor will reprise her role as Katniss Everdeen in the latest installment of the franchise, which is set for release in theaters next month, and will star alongside two other Hunger Games original cast members: Josh Hutcherson as Peeta Mellark and Woody Harrelson as Haymitch Abernathy.

Speaking on the Call Her Daddy podcast, Lawrence called the experience "unbelievable" and "so emotional."

"Josh and I didn't walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other, it was so beautiful," she said.

The news of Lawrence and Hutcherson's return was reported by multiple outlets in December 2025, but wasn't officially confirmed until today — and neither actor appears in the movie's trailer .

Nothing is known about their roles; they're expected to be small and potentially appear in a flash-forward, Variety reported last year.

It has been three years since viewers last caught up with the citizens of Panem. The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes , which did not feature Lawrence or Hutcherson, kicked off the prequel era, telling the story of what happened before Katniss and Peeta's Games. The Ballad movie rewound 64 years to follow a young Coriolanus Snow, and next up, it's Haymitch Abernathy's turn in Sunrise on the Reaping .

An adaptation of Suzanne Collins's bestselling book of the same name, Sunrise on the Reaping , in theaters Nov. 20, covers the 50th Hunger Games — the second Quarter Quell. In the movie, audiences will understand how Haymitch goes from an unwilling participant in the Games to the surly mentor that Katniss and Peeta meet nearly two and a half decades later. Up-and-coming actor Joseph Zada plays 16-year-old Haymitch.

Other key cast members include Ralph Fiennes as the third actor to play Snow, after Donald Sutherland and Tom Blyth, and Elle Fanning as a young Effie Trinket, a role previously held by Elizabeth Banks. Glenn Close, Maya Hawke, Jesse Plemons and Mckenna Grace also feature.

articles.title: Manoj Bajpayee on how making the first move led to 'Raajneeti', 'Gangs Of Wasseypur' and 'Special 26': 'I saw some lows, refused films and wasn't happy'
articles.summary: Manoj Bajpayee is spending his days calling younger directors, hoping to be part of their stories and begin a new chapter that makes him feel “alive”.
articles.body: Manoj Bajpayee is spending his days calling younger directors, hoping to be part of their stories and begin a new chapter that makes him feel “alive”. The ‘Satya’ and ‘The Family Man’ actor says this habit is helping him build a filmography he can be proud of.Manoj Bajpayee’s morning routineExplaining his approach in an interview with News18, Manoj Bajpayee said, “That’s how I’m approaching my days. Every morning I wake up and make it a point to call at least one director. It’s not a bad practice. I’m more interested in building a glorious and fascinating filmography than doing a series of films, back-to-back, in a year. I want to feel proud of my body of work. That’s why I’m always on the lookout for directors, new and old.”Making it easier for new filmmakersAccording to the actor, this routine also gives aspiring filmmakers easier access to him. He said, “I call them and let them know that I’m available and that I’m excited with the prospect of working with them. Sometimes, the new ones can’t find a way to reach out to me. If they hear from me first, the process becomes so much easier for them.”How the first move changed his careerTaking the first step is also how Manoj got films like ‘Raajneeti’, ‘Gangs Of Wasseypur’ and ‘Special 26’, which marked a major turn in his career. Recalling the period before them, he said, “Before these films, I saw some lows. The kind of work that I wanted to do wasn’t coming my way. All I was doing was refusing films and saying no to people. And the ones I said yes to, I wasn’t happy doing those films.”The ‘A Wednesday’ connectionManoj then spoke about watching ‘A Wednesday’, which led to conversations with several filmmakers. "That’s when I watched A Wednesday. Neeraj (Pandey) and I had met after that, and we spoke about cinema at large. He told me how he makes his films. That’s all I remember from that chat. I also remember meeting Prakash (Jha) ji at around the same time. Anurag (Kashyap) and I were talking simultaneously. Those films started happening to me a year after those meetings," he added.More about Manoj BajpayeeOn the work front, Manoj Bajpayee was recently seen in the film 'Gajab Raat'. articles.body: Amy Grant is opening up about her relationship with her husband, Vince Gill, after over 20 years of marriage, saying he will always stand up for her. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 65-year-old singer touched on her marriage to Gill, noting that while he is "kind, kind, kind," he will do anything to protect her. "He does have a toggle switch, and if somebody does something to throw that switch, he can respond so quickly," she said. "And so he can see the field, and he's got a quick mind. And he is not afraid to put somebody in their place or be protective. And so, yeah, I mean, I feel so loved by him." In March, Gill told the story of the time he confronted host Don Imus while on his radio show, and called him out for talking negatively about him and Grant. AMY GRANT'S EMOTIONAL ACCOUNT OF DOCTORS AND NURSES SINGING OUTSIDE DOLLY PARTON'S HOSPITAL ROOM He told the "Naked Lunch" podcast that Imus started out as a fan of his, but after he married Grant the radio host changed his tune and would say things such as, "Vince Gill, lost the Baby Jesus, married that Christian girl." While on his radio show, Gill waited until Grant's name came up and then took his chance to stand up for his wife. "I said, ‘Well, if you ever met her, you'd never say an unkind word about her,’" Gill said. "‘I'm going to shoot you straight.’ I said, ‘I really only came on this show for one reason.’ I said, ‘We're either going to talk this out, straighten this out,’ I said, 'or I'm going to crawl across this desk, and I'm going to kick your a--.'" Gill noted that on his way home from the interview, he caught Imus on the air and heard him say, "I don't know why I was giving that guy so much crap. I love that guy," adding that the two of them stayed friends until Imus' death in December 2019. articles.title: CBSE Kochi Sahodaya School arts festival begins today
articles.summary: CBSE Kochi Sahodaya arts fest Utsav 2026 begins in Kochi with 3,500+ students from 42 schools, 140 events, held Thu-Sat at two venues in Thiruvaniyoor.
articles.body: Kochi: More than 3,500 students from 42 schools are expected to participate in Utsav 2026, the CBSE Kochi Sahodaya School Complex arts festival, to be held from Thursday to Saturday at Cochin Refineries School and Global Public School in Thiruvaniyoor.Film director Jude Anthany Joseph will inaugurate the three-day festival at the auditorium of Global Public School at 9am. Cochin Refineries School principal and president of Kochi Sahodaya, Vinumon K Mathew, will preside over the inaugural function.General convener Dileep George said all arrangements had been completed. The festival will feature competitions in 140 events.“To make it easier for students to participate, we have chosen two neighbouring schools as venues. Shuttle services will be arranged between the schools to facilitate the movement of students and teachers. articles.title: Serie A official line-ups: Milan vs. Bologna
articles.summary: Alphadjo Cisse, Omari Hutchinson and Davide Bartesaghi support Goncalo Ramos upfront, as Milan host a Bologna side with Samuel Mbangula and Federico Bernarde...
articles.body:
Alphadjo Cisse, Omari Hutchinson and Davide Bartesaghi support Goncalo Ramos upfront, as Milan host a Bologna side with Samuel Mbangula and Federico Bernardeschi.

It kicks off at 18:30 CET [17:30 GMT] at San Siro, with Juan Luca Sacchi refereeing.

Milan are still unbeaten in Serie A under Rúben Amorim. They sit fifth on 18 points after Sunday's 2-0 win at Udinese , which steadied things after a 3-0 Europa League defeat at Bournemouth. Lazio's 6-2 win at Sassuolo on Tuesday put them seven points clear of the Rossoneri, and Saturday's Derby della Madonnina against Inter is next on Amorim's schedule.

BOLOGNA, ITALY – OCTOBER 17: Tommaso Pobega of Bologna FC 1909 celebrates with teammates after scoring his team's first goal during the Serie A match between Bologna FC and FC Internazionale at Stadio Renato Dall'Ara on October 17, 2026 in Bologna, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images)

Bologna arrive 13th on eight points but have won their last two away games, at Lecce and Cagliari. Raffaele Palladino replaced Domenico Tedesco in September. Tommaso Pobega is back at San Siro after leaving Milan for the Rossoblù in 2025.

Milan's injury list keeps growing. Ruben Loftus-Cheek is the latest addition after a medial hamstring tear in his left thigh. Adrien Rabiot (right calf fatigue), Diego Moreira (hamstring fatigue) and Mario Gila (ankle overload) are still out, and all three are aiming to be back for the derby.

Samuel Chukwueze (hip), Matteo Gabbia (hamstring), Alexis Saelemaekers (ankle surgery) and Pietro Terracciano (muscular) are also unavailable. Mike Maignan's red card at Bournemouth only applies in the Europa League.

ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan, gives instructions to Adrien Rabiot during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Atalanta BC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 18, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Bologna are without Riccardo Orsolini, Roberto Piccoli and Emil Holm, who all have hamstring injuries. Jay Enem (Achilles tendinopathy) and Lorenzo De Silvestri (right hamstring) are not in the squad.

Milan: Maignan; Tomori, De Winter, Pavlovic, Estupinan; Musah, Jashari; Hutchinson, Cisse, Bartesaghi; Ramos

Bologna: Skorupski; Darmian, Casale, Theate; Zortea, Ferguson, Pobega, Alhassane; Bernardeschi, Odgaard, Mbangula

articles.title: Serie A official line-ups: Venezia vs. Inter
articles.summary: Ange-Yoan Bonny partners Marcus Thuram in attack for Inter against Venezia, whilst Davide Nicola sticks with under-fire striker Akor Adams in his front line...
articles.body:
Ange-Yoan Bonny partners Marcus Thuram in attack for Inter against Venezia, whilst Davide Nicola sticks with under-fire striker Akor Adams in his front line for the hosts.

It kicks off at 18:30 CET [17:30 GMT] at the Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo, with Luca Pairetto refereeing.

Inter need three points to draw level with Lazio again at the top of Serie A . Gennaro Gattuso's side moved three points clear on 25 with their 6-2 win at Sassuolo last night. Cristian Chivu's side came from behind to beat Fiorentina 2-1 on Sunday, with Marcus Thuram and Piotr Zieliński both scoring in stoppage time. Saturday's derby against Milan is next.

Venezia are bottom with three points. They beat Napoli in Davide Nicola's first game in charge, but lost 1-0 at Genoa on Sunday .

VENICE, ITALY – OCTOBER 17: Filip Stankovic of Venezia FC celebrates during the Serie A match between Venezia FC and SSC Napoli at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on October 17, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images)

The game has a family subplot. Venezia goalkeeper Filip Stanković came through the Inter academy, and the Nerazzurri kept a 50% sell-on clause when they sold him in 2024. His younger brother Aleksandar is in the Inter squad, and their father Dejan won the Treble at the club.

Lautaro Martínez (hamstring) and Luis Henrique (adductor) are both out until after the international break. Benjamin Pavard (adductor), Curtis Jones (adductor) and John Stones (hamstring) are also missing. Pavard and Jones are hoping to be fit for next Tuesday's Champions League game.

Venezia are without Thierry Correia (hamstring), Marin Šverko (hip), Andrea Adorante (back surgery) and Bartol Franjić (shoulder surgery).

MILAN, ITALY – OCTOBER 25: Cristian Chivu looks on before the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and ACF Fiorentina at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 25, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)
